agree.reason: The page is warm and believable, but an owner who pays her cousin $600 a year sees $199 a month and nothing telling her she can keep him, so she probably won't book the call.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief, but the heading 'Clean books lower your accountant's bill' turns what 9 of 31 clients reported into a general promise, and leaving out last year's 3 missed deadlines makes 'your books will be closed by the 10th' sound firmer than the record supports.

works_the_facts.reason: Comparing the $800 saving to more than four months of fees is correct and works in the writer's favour, but the page never works out the yearly cost, a retention rate such as 29 of 31, or what the saving would mean for someone paying $600.

right_comparison.reason: The only alternative shown is vague messy books that an accountant has to fix; this reader's real alternative is a cousin she likes who charges $600 at tax time, and the page never says that her accountant keeps doing her taxes.

qualification.reason: The late-month guarantee names a date (the 10th) and a consequence the reader can check (that month is free), but it doesn't say when it began or admit that the deadline has been missed before.

objections.reason: The objections that matter to her (the cost against $600, and whether she'd have to drop her cousin) are left unanswered, and the page also leaves out facts that would help: no contract, 30 days' notice to stop, and why the price went up.

fit.reason: It's close to the 350 words asked for, it reads as main sales-page copy with clear sections, and it ends with the booking button.
